Accountable obligation owner.value: Filing determination owner; escalation to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — each state's rate/form filing statute + that state's SERFF General Instructions and Product Requirements Locator entry re-read at determination time (rep: Oklahoma Title 36)

In-scope processes.value: Product development change intake → filing determination gate, for every form, rate, rule and manual change across the 50 SERFF jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Filing Access + state filing-rules pages; determinations logged in the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Filing Determination Procedure (pre-use gate) — intake, classification, per-state review-method lookup, exemption basis, deemer math, log entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Chief Compliance Officer; reviewed annually and on any state filing-rule bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — determination must close before the product build freeze; prior-approval states drive the latest-submission date backed off the target effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker milestone alerts at T-90/T-60/T-30 days to target effective date for every open determination

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filing determination log entry + dated screenshot of the state's filing rules retained 7 years from the form/rate withdrawal date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any change implemented without a determination is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every 'no filing required' call and every late/unfiled remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All product/form/rate/rule changes implemented in the quarter per the policy admin change log, across all writing companies and states

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any implemented change with no determination on file before its effective date is a fail; ≥1 fail escalates to the CCO

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-filing; test runs quarterly over that quarter's population plus 100% review of prior-approval states

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored any sampled determination

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing-determination test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export + SERFF tracking numbers + approval letters, presentable as a market conduct exam response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns the exam/inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of an unfiled change before it is sent

checklist.step: Pull the approved change request from the product change queue and record product name, writing company, TOI/Sub-TOI, target effective date and the list of affected states.

Classify each element of the change as FORM (policy form, endorsement, application, rider, notice), RATE (base rates, factors, tiers, territory relativities), RULE (eligibility/underwriting rules, manual pages) or NON-FILED (marketing collateral, internal procedure).
Collect the source artifacts from Product Development and Pricing — form PDFs with form number and edition date on every page, rate exhibits, rule manual pages, and the actuarial support file.
In SERFF, open Filing Rules for each affected state (Instructions ▸ Filing Rules, or the state's Product Requirements Locator entry) and read the current General Instructions for the TOI.
Record the state's review method for this change type: PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE, INFORMATIONAL/FILE-FOR-RECORD or EXEMPT — one determination per state per change element.
Confirm the TOI and Sub-TOI codes against the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix for the line, and confirm the state accepts that TOI through SERFF (some lines file outside SERFF).

Where the answer is 'no filing required', record the specific statutory or bulletin basis for the exemption (e.g. commercial large-risk exemption, exempt commercial purchaser, non-filed inland marine) — never an unsupported 'not required'.

Search SERFF Filing Access for prior approved filings by form number, TOI and company to see whether an existing approval already covers the change; capture the prior SERFF tracking number if reuse applies.
Read the state's review/deemer clock (e.g. 30, 45 or 60 days) and back-solve the latest submission date from the target effective date, adding the internal package-prep lead time.

List the companion items each state will demand with the filing — actuarial memorandum and certification, rate/rule schedule, Statement of Variability, readability (Flesch) certification, side-by-side redline, third-party filer authorization — so the package scope is fixed at determination time.

Write the determination row per state into the Filing Determination Log: change id, state, element, filing required Y/N, review method, filing type, statutory cite, deemer days, latest submission date, decider and date.
Route every 'no filing required' determination and every prior-approval state to Regulatory Counsel for sign-off before the log row is closed.
Publish the determination back onto the product change record and set the go-live gate: prior-approval states cannot be released until an approval or satisfied deemer is recorded.
Escalate to the Chief Compliance Officer when the target effective date cannot survive the state's review timeline, so the date is moved rather than the filing skipped.
Retain the determination log entry, the dated state filing-rules screenshots and counsel sign-off for 7 years after the form or rate is withdrawn.

testing.step: Extract the population: every product/form/rate/rule change implemented in the quarter from the policy administration change log, by writing company and state.
Reconcile the population to the Filing Determination Log — every implemented change must have a determination row dated before its effective date; unmatched changes are automatic exceptions.
Select the sample: 100% of prior-approval-state changes plus 25 randomly selected changes from the remaining population (minimum 40 rows total).
Re-perform the review-method call for each sampled state/change against the current SERFF Filing Rules page and the state's General Instructions; any differing conclusion is an exception.
Verify the TOI/Sub-TOI recorded on the determination matches the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix entry for the product.
For every 'no filing required' determination in the sample, confirm a specific statutory or bulletin cite plus Regulatory Counsel sign-off exists.
For every 'filing required' determination, trace to the SERFF tracking number and confirm the submission (or the reused prior approval) pre-dates the implementation date in SERFF Filing Access.
Recompute the deemer/latest-submission math on 10 sampled filings and confirm the release gate held for prior-approval states (no go-live before approval or satisfied deemer).
Log every exception in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with root cause, owner and remediation date; retest remediated items in the following quarter.
Independent reviewer signs the workpaper with the exception rate against the zero-unfiled-change threshold and reports results to the Compliance Committee.
